title: Fuzzy RDD: imperfect compliance with admission cutoff

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Fuzzy Regression–Discontinuity Design (FRDD).  
• Running variable: centred GPA (running_var – 0.50).  
• Cut-off: 0.50 (corresponds to GPA = 3.0).  
• Instrument (z): eligibility indicator (1 = GPA ≥ cut-off).  
Because some students below the cut-off are treated and some above it are not, eligibility serves as an exogenous instrument for actual scholarship receipt.  

Key assumptions  
1. Continuity: In the absence of treatment, potential graduation outcomes vary smoothly in GPA at the cut-off.  
2. First-stage relevance: Eligibility sharply changes the probability of receiving the scholarship.  
3. Exclusion / Local Randomisation: Near the cut-off, eligibility affects graduation only through scholarship receipt (no other channels).  
4. Monotonicity: No student becomes less likely to receive the scholarship solely because she became eligible.  

Under these assumptions, a 2SLS/IV regression using eligibility as the instrument identifies the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) of the scholarship for compliers at the GPA threshold.

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################
# Fuzzy RDD: Scholarship & Graduation
# -----------------------------------------
# Requirements: readr, dplyr, AER, sandwich,
#               lmtest, rdrobust
############################################
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(rdrobust)

# 1. Read data -------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s30_data.csv",
               col_types = cols())

# 2. Construct variables ---------------------------------------------------
cutoff <- 0.5                          # stated cut-off in normalised GPA
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    z        = ifelse(running_var >= cutoff, 1, 0),  # instrument
    run_c    = running_var - cutoff                  # centre at cut-off
  )

# Primary bandwidth supplied by author
df_bw <- df %>% filter(near_cutoff == 1)

# 3. Main FRDD estimate (local linear IV) ----------------------------------
iv_main <- ivreg(y ~ treated + run_c,
                 ~ z + run_c,
                 data = df_bw)

robust_main <- coeftest(iv_main,
                        vcov = vcovHC(iv_main, type = "HC1"))

cat("\n================  MAIN RESULT  ================\n")
print(robust_main["treated", ])
cat("------------------------------------------------\n")

# 4. Diagnostics / first-stage strength ------------------------------------
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic:\n")
print(summary(iv_main, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics[1, ])

# 5. Robustness checks -----------------------------------------------------
## (a) Higher-order polynomial within same bandwidth
iv_quad <- ivreg(y ~ treated + run_c + I(run_c^2),
                 ~ z + run_c + I(run_c^2),
                 data = df_bw)
robust_quad <- coeftest(iv_quad,
                        vcov = vcovHC(iv_quad, type = "HC1"))

## (b) Wider bandwidth (whole sample)
iv_full <- ivreg(y ~ treated + run_c,
                 ~ z + run_c,
                 data = df)
robust_full <- coeftest(iv_full,
                        vcov = vcovHC(iv_full, type = "HC1"))

## (c) Non-parametric rdrobust
rd_out <- rdrobust(y = df$y,
                   x = df$run_c,
                   c = 0,
                   fuzzy = df$treated)

# 6. Print robustness summary ---------------------------------------------
cat("\n========== ROBUSTNESS: Polynomial ==========\n")
print(robust_quad["treated", ])

cat("\n========== ROBUSTNESS: Full Sample =========\n")
print(robust_full["treated", ])

cat("\n========== ROBUSTNESS: rdrobust ============\n")
print(rd_out$coef)       # column 1 = τ̂ (fuzzy point estimate)

############################################
# End of script
############################################
```

The script  
• reads the dataset,  
• creates the eligibility instrument,  
• runs a local-linear 2SLS within the author-defined bandwidth,  
• prints the LATE estimate with heteroskedasticity-robust SEs and the first-stage F-statistic, and  
• reports three robustness checks: quadratic control-function, wider bandwidth, and a non-parametric rdrobust estimate.

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition and prior literature suggest that need-based financial aid increases on-time graduation. Therefore:  
• Sign: positive.  
• Magnitude: roughly +0.15 – 0.25 (15–25 percentage-point increase in 4-year graduation probability for compliers at the 3.0 GPA threshold).  
Given imperfect compliance, the first-stage jump should be sizeable (≥ 0.4), producing a clearly identifiable LATE with an F-stat > 10.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Fuzzy RDD — eligibility cutoff as IV for scholarship receipt; LATE = ITT / first-stage jump
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Scholarship receipt significantly improves graduation rates for compliers
_ground_truth.main_effect: ~25pp graduation rate increase (LATE via fuzzy RDD)
